headline: Found The Cellar at 14 Mill Street in violation for overservice of alcohol, with a one-day suspension held in abeyance.
summary: The hearing concerned an August 22 incident in which a punch was thrown outside and a gunshot was fired in the parking garage. Officers said they could not link the shooting to the bar. The commission also approved permits for two October events and Sunday brunch hours at Hill City, and referred Hill City's change of category to a public hearing.

Page 1 
 
Monty Tech                    BOARD OF LICENSE COMMISSIONERS 
         City Hall, 718 Main Street 
              Fitchburg MA  01420 
              (978) 829-1820    
  
Daniel Sarefield, Chairman        
Richard Boscardin 
Glenn Fossa 
MINUTES OF MEETING 
A regular meeting of the Board of License Commissioners was held on Monday, October 5 10, 2026, called to 
order by Commissioner Sarefield at 6:00 PM. Commissioner Boscardin and Commissioner Fossa were present. 
FPD Liaison Lt. Christopher Bellofatto was present and Officer Michael Sevigny. Assistant City Clerk 
Elizabeth McNiff were present.  
I. REVIEW AND APPROVAL OF MINUTES OF PRIOR MEETING(S) 
Regular Minutes and Executive Minutes of September 14, 2026.  
The regular and executive minutes of September 14, 2026 were approved by roll call vote 3/0.  
 
II. NEW APPLICATIONS 
Please note that the Commission may enter into Executive Session pursuant to G.L. c. 30A, sec. 21(a) 
(5) (Discussion of CORI results), if required during this portion of the agenda, and will return to 
regular session upon completion. 
 
 Monday – Saturday Entertainment Permit  
Michael Talarico, New Players Theatre Guild, Halloween Party Fundraiser, 15 Rollstone Street, 
Saturday October 17, 2026, from 8:00 PM – 1:00 AM, for DJ and dancing, for approximately 50 
people.   
Mr. Talarico was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application and verified 
that Mr. Talarico is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Applications approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.  
Jainny Andrews, Civic Days Committee, Trick or Treat on Main, 904 Main Street, Upper Common, 
Saturday, October 24, 2026 for DJ, from 10:00 AM to 4:00 PM, for approximately 1000 people.  
Ms. Andrews was present at the meeting. Commissioner reviewed the application and verified that Ms. 
Andrews is aware that all entertainment must be shut down thirty minutes prior to closing. Ms. Andrews 
shared that it would be the same set up as years past.   
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.
Page 2 
 
Special One Day All Alcoholic Beverages 
Michael Talarico, New Players Theatre Guild, Halloween Party Fundraiser, 15 Rollstone Street, 
Saturday October 17, 2026, from 8:00 PM – 1:00 AM, for approximately 50 people.   
Mr. Talarico was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application and verified 
that the events will have TIP certified servers. Commissioner Sarefield stated that all serving of alcohol 
must be ceased thirty minutes prior to closing. Commissioner Sarefield asked if this was a ticketed 
event, Mr. Talarico stated it was not, tickets will be sold at the door.  
No concerns from Lt. Bellofatto. 
Applications approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.  
Application for Change of Category (i.e., All Alcohol/Wine, Malt)  
Nacoro Inc. DBA Hill City, 299 Lunenburg Street  
(Referred to public hearing on November 2, 2026)  
Application for Sunday Brunch Hours  
Nacoro Inc. DBA Hill City, 299 Lunenburg Street  
Mr. Lamoureux was present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield reviewed the application. Mr. 
Lamoureux stated that he was applying for this because customers had showed interest in having 
beverages earlier on Sundays.  
Application approved by unanimous roll call vote 3/0.  
 
III. SUMMONS HEARING  
The Cellar – 14 Mill Street 
Mr. Roy and his doorman, Mr. Adam Bergeron, were present at the meeting. Commissioner Sarefield 
opened the hearing by explaining the process, which would begin with a presentation by the reporting 
officers, followed by questions for the reporting officers from the Board. Then the licensee would be 
given the opportunity to ask questions as well, and then to present a defense, introduce any witnesses, 
and any mitigating information. When the evidentiary phase ended, the Board would deliberate in the 
open meeting and, if warranted, vote on the finding of a violation or violations and, if a violation was 
found to have occurred, vote on sanctions.    
 
Officer George and Officer Monaghan, whose reports had been submitted to the Commission, were also 
present. Lieutenant Bellofatto began by summarizing the reports concerning an incident that occurred 
on August 22, 2026. 
Officer George’s report indicated that he encountered an intoxicated female patron near her vehicle in 
the parking lot who had vomited. The patron stated that she was waiting for an Uber and had come from 
The Cellar. Officer George remained with the patron to ensure she was not left alone while waiting for 
her ride. 
While responding to the area, Officer Monaghan encountered a disturbance in the lower parking garage 
involving individuals striking a vehicle occupied by other people. During the incident, Officer George 
heard a gunshot and screaming and went to assist Officer Monaghan. 
 
Lieutenant Bellofatto presented several video recordings to the Commission, most of which had been 
provided by the licensee, along with additional footage obtained from a member of the public. The 
footage showed an unprovoked punch being thrown by one patron at another in the outdoor area of the
Page 3 
establishment. While viewing the footage, Mr. Roy stated that neither he nor the other employees 
working that evening recognized the individual in the garage incident as someone who had been inside 
the establishment. Mr. Bergeron stated that he had observed the individual and a group of people in the 
parking lot prior to the incident.  
Commissioner Sarefield asked whether the officers had anything further to add. Officer Monaghan 
stated that he had been actively patrolling the area that evening, which was within his assigned patrol 
area. He was on his way to assist Officer George with the intoxicated female patron in the parking lot. 
Shortly thereafter, he heard a commotion in the lower parking garage and went to investigate. Officer 
Monaghan stated that the incident in the garage remained under active investigation and that he could 
not provide additional details. The officers had heard distressed screaming and observed individuals 
damaging a vehicle before a male individual produced a firearm and fired into the crowd. 
Commissioner Sarefield confirmed that Officer George had initially been attending to the intoxicated 
patron before responding to the disturbance in the lower parking garage. Officer George confirmed that 
this was correct. Commissioner Sarefield emphasized that the Commission needed to distinguish 
between three separate incidents: the intoxicated patron found in the parking garage, the assault that 
occurred in the outdoor area of the establishment, and the shooting in the parking garage. 
 
Commissioner Fossa commended the officers for their work that evening. Referring to the police 
reports, he asked whether it had been determined if a canned beverage found in the parking lot had 
originated from the establishment. The Fitchburg Police Department could not confirm the source of the 
beverage. Commissioner Fossa stated that, based on the video footage presented and Lieutenant 
Bellofatto’ s review, there was no indication that the individual involved in the shooting had come from 
The Cellar. He also noted that the intoxicated female patron found in the parking garage had stated that 
she had come from The Cellar. Commissioner Boscardin had no questions at that time. 
 
Commissioner Sarefield returned to the assault shown in the outdoor video footage and asked how long 
the individuals had been in the area. Based on the footage and information provided by employees 
working that evening, one individual had been outside for some time, while the other had been inside the 
establishment for a period of time. Commissioner Sarefield asked whether the individual involved in the 
shooting had been arrested and whether he had been inside The Cellar before the incident. Lieutenant 
Bellofatto stated that, based on the investigation to that point, there was no indication that the individual 
had been inside the establishment. 
 
The hearing was then turned over to Mr. Roy. He thanked the officers for their work and stated that the 
events of that evening were not something he ever wanted to see happen again. Mr. Roy confirmed that 
he had contacted the Fitchburg Police Department that evening because of concerns about increased 
loitering in the parking lot. He added that employees had recently observed empty beverage cans in the 
area. Mr. Roy provided the Commission with signed, sworn statements from each employee who had 
been working that evening, documenting their accounts of the events. He stated that he could not 
confirm whether the individuals involved in the parking garage incident had come from other 
establishments. Mr. Roy asked whether the female patron had indicated that she visited other 
establishments before arriving at The Cellar. Officer George stated that she had not provided details 
about the rest of her evening and had only stated that she had come from The Cellar. 
 
Commissioner Sarefield asked whether Mr. Roy had anything further to present or ask. Mr. Roy 
reiterated that he had provided the employee statements for the Commission’s review. He also stated 
that, following the incident, he had implemented changes to the establishment’s rules and procedures, 
including ending last call earlier than required by the license. Commissioner Sarefield then announced 
that the hearing would move into the deliberation phase.
Page 4 
Commissioner Sarefield stated that incidents of this nature at licensed establishments were concerning. 
He asked whether there was any evidence connecting the shooting to activity inside The Cellar. 
Commissioner Fossa stated that he did not see a connection between the shooting and the establishment. 
He noted that the Commission had encountered similar incidents involving other establishments during 
his time serving on the Commission. He also observed that Mr. Roy had been present and actively 
involved that evening, had made phone calls, and appeared to have responded as appropriately as 
possible under the circumstances. Commissioner Sarefield asked whether the police could establish a 
connection between the assault in the outdoor area and the shooting in the parking garage. The officers 
stated that they could not establish such a connection, as no individuals identified as being associated 
with The Cellar appeared to be connected to the shooting. 
 
Commissioner Fossa stated that the punch shown in the video appeared to have been addressed quickly 
and brought under control, particularly when compared with other incidents the Commission had 
reviewed in recent months. Commissioner Sarefield stated that he did not observe any clear indication 
of intoxication among the individuals shown in the video footage. He asked whether the other 
commissioners observed any evidence that the licensee had failed to fulfill his responsibilities. 
Commissioners Boscardin and Sarefield stated that they did not. 
 
Commissioner Sarefield also asked Lieutenant Bellofatto whether his review indicated that anyone 
involved in the incidents had been overserved. Lieutenant Bellofatto stated that there was nothing in the 
information reviewed to indicate that the individuals involved in the other incidents had been 
overserved. Commissioner Sarefield noted that Mr. Roy had responded promptly to the assault and had 
taken proactive steps when the shooting occurred. He emphasized the licensee’s responsibility to help 
ensure public safety at his establishment. Mr. Roy stated that the punch appeared to have been a sucker 
punch and that it was addressed quickly, with no prior indication that a fight was developing. 
 
Commissioner Sarefield welcomed the operational changes Mr. Roy had implemented since the incident. 
Mr. Roy stated that the establishment had recently reduced its operating hours and introduced a cover 
charge. The Commission then returned to the incident involving the intoxicated female patron found in 
the parking garage. Commissioner Sarefield stated that, if the patron had been served at The Cellar and 
was found intoxicated at approximately 1:00 AM, the Commission needed to consider whether a 
violation had occurred. Commissioner Fossa stated that the patron had been served at the 
establishment. Mr. Roy responded that he had not previously been made aware of the patron’s presence 
in the parking garage or the number of beverages she had consumed. He stated that this was the first 
time he had received this information and that he could not provide a response regarding the specific 
circumstances. Commissioner Fossa requested additional input from the police. Lieutenant Bellofatto 
stated that he could not confirm whether the patron had visited other establishments before arriving at 
The Cellar. However, she had stated that she came from The Cellar, and she had consumed enough 
alcohol to become ill in the parking lot. He could not confirm the amount of alcohol she had consumed 
at the establishment. Commissioner Sarefield referred the matter back to the Commission to determine 
whether a violation had occurred.  
 
Commissioner Fossa made a motion to find The Cellar in violation of overservice of alcohol. The 
motion was approved unanimously by roll call vote 3/0.  
 
Following the finding of a violation, Commissioner Sarefield stated that the Commission would need to 
determine an appropriate sanction. Commissioners Fossa and Boscardin took into consideration the 
operational changes implemented by the establishment following the incident. Commissioner Fossa 
emphasized the importance of treating all licensees fairly and consistently when determining sanctions 
for incidents at licensed establishments. He noted that, in this first summons hearing, Mr. Roy had
Page 5 
provided sworn written statements from his employees and demonstrated that he had implemented 
additional procedures. 
 
Commissioner Fossa made a motion to impose a one-day suspension, held in abeyance until December 
31, 2026. The motion was approved unanimously by roll call vote 3/0. 
 
IV. OLD BUSINESS  
The Boulder Café – Liquor License Status Review  
Ms. McNamara was present at the meeting and informed the Commission that she no longer had a 
lease at 880 Main Street. She inquired about her options for obtaining a pocket license. Commissioner 
Sarefield explained that she could hold a pocket license for up to six months; however, with the liquor 
license renewal period approaching, she would be unable to sign the renewal package without securing 
a new location. Ms. McNamara stated that she is actively searching for a new space. If she is unable to 
secure a location before the renewal paperwork must be signed, she will surrender her license and 
reapply for a new license once she has secured a new location. 
 
 
V. CORRESPONDENCE  
   
 
 
VI. NEW BUSINESS 
   
 
NEXT REGULAR MEETING 
 
 
Monday, October 19, 2026 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:59 PM 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Joanna Bilotta, City Clerk
